accepted_notes.2026-10-26: Exclusions re-verified against the artefacts that actually ship, not just the lockfile. undici 7.30.0 and vitest 4.1.11 are dev=true in package-lock and reachable only through jsdom / test tooling, and no application source imports either, so neither can reach the browser bundle. tailwindcss 3.4.19 was misclassified: it sat in package.json dependencies, so a `npm ci --omit=dev` install pulled it in and the frontend image carried it. Fixed in this pass: tailwindcss moved to devDependencies (it is a PostCSS compiler executed during the build - nothing imports it at runtime, only the generated CSS ships) and frontend/Dockerfile now runs `npm prune --omit=dev` after `next build`, so the runtime image holds production dependencies only. Verified in the built image: undici, vitest, jsdom and tailwindcss are all absent, 302 packages remain, the next CLI still resolves, and the image serves GET / -> 200. The browser bundle (.next/static) contains none of the three. tailwindcss's own advisories stay deferred: the fix is tailwind 4.x, a major that breaks the current API.
accepted_notes.2026-10-25: Accepted from the audit artifact of run 40180100538. undici (high) is dev-only: package-lock marks every undici dependency path dev=true, reached solely through jsdom -> vitest, so it never ships. @vitest/*, vitest are dev tooling. tailwindcss (moderate, via postcss-nested / postcss-selector-parser) is build-time CSS tooling; its fix is tailwind 4.3.3, a major that breaks the current API, so it is deferred to a deliberate upgrade rather than bundled into this push.
